title: Shared tray transport and discharge
summary: The two Pandas hold one tray between them. Each arm's small open fork cradles a tab on one end of the tray, and an orange ball lies loose in the tray. Working together, the arms must first hold the tray steadily. They then carry it through two waypoints that make a turn. When the environment pushes the ball, they must bring it back to rest near the tray centre. Next they bring the tray to an exit position beside a fixed basin, and finally they tip the ball out so that it settles in the basin. Both forks must support the tray during the transport phases, the ball must not leave the tray before the discharge, and the tray must never drop low.
robot_setup: panda-0 (left): base at (-0.55, -0.22, 0), yaw 0 (facing +x). panda-1 (right): base at (0.74, 0.22, 0), yaw pi (facing -x). Each carries a support fork: a small, shallow square cradle 0.07 m x 0.07 m inside (2 x `tool_half`, `tool_half` = 0.035 m). It has a 5 mm floor and 18 mm high walls on three sides, is open on the tool +x side, and is held by an adapter on its closed tool -x wall. The tool frame is the centre of the cradle floor's top surface, z up. The TCP sits 0.12 m along tool -x and 0.04 m above the tool frame. Left fork start: (-0.075, 0, 0.22), orientation identity (open side toward world +x). Right fork start: (0.215, 0, 0.22), quaternion (0, 0, 0, 1) (yawed 180 deg, open side toward world -x). The two open sides face each other. In this task both arms' servos plan their reference motion with lower acceleration and jerk fractions than usual (0.30 and 0.025, default 0.55 and 0.05). Role labels in every phase: panda-0 left_support, panda-1 right_support.
scene: A blue rigid tray, 0.20 m x 0.24 m inside, has a 9 mm rim and a 5 mm floor. A flat tab (48 mm x 60 mm, 8 mm thick) sticks out at floor level from the middle of each of its two longer sides. At the start each tab rests in one arm's fork, so the tray hangs between the two arms. An orange ball (radius 18 mm) lies loose near the middle of the tray. A fixed blue open-top basin, 0.21 m x 0.20 m inside and 0.08 m deep, stands on posts above the table. Nothing moves by itself, except that the environment gives the ball a brief push along world +x the moment the third phase begins. The table top is the world's z = 0 plane.
scene_privileged: Tray: free rigid body, mass 0.25 kg, friction 0.3, restitution 0.05. Its frame origin is the centre of its floor's top surface. Inner half-size is 0.10 (x) x 0.12 (y) m, the rim is 9 mm high, and the walls and floor are 5 mm thick. The tabs are 0.048 x 0.060 x 0.008 m, centred at tray-frame (+-0.125, 0, 0), so they span |x| from 0.101 to 0.149 m. At reset the tray is at (0.07, 0, 0.225), identity orientation, at rest. The tab undersides are then 1 mm above the fork floors; the left tab spans world x in [-0.079, -0.031] and the right tab x in [0.171, 0.219]. Ball: radius `radius` = 0.018 m, mass `object_mass` = 0.035 kg, restitution 0.05, friction 0.2. At reset it is at rest at (0.07 + u, 0, 0.244), 1 mm above the tray floor, with u drawn uniformly in [-0.006, 0.006] m. Push: for the first 0.03 s after phase disturbance_recovery begins, a constant force of `disturbance_impulse` / 0.03 = 0.233 N acts along world +x at the ball's centre. The total impulse is `disturbance_impulse` = 0.007 N s. Basin: static container with floor top surface centre at (0.30, 0.18, 0.08); inner half-size 0.105 (x) x 0.10 (y) m; wall height 0.08 m (rim at z = 0.16); friction 0.4; restitution 0.03. Forks: `tool_half` = 0.035, `tool_mass` = 0.12 kg, `tool_friction` = 0.3, restitution 0.05. Horizon `horizon` = 25 s. The only random draw is u, made at reset.

phases.name: shared_support
phases.text: For 0.35 s without interruption, two things hold. The tray is supported by both forks: it has been in contact with the left fork within the last 0.04 s and with the right fork within the last 0.04 s. And the ball is inside the tray, as defined under ball_spill.

phases.name: transport_turn
phases.text: With the tray supported by both forks (as above), the tray's frame origin (the centre of its floor's top surface) comes within 0.025 m of waypoint A = (0.12, -0.04, 0.27). Later, again with both forks supporting it, the origin comes within 0.025 m of waypoint B = (0.02, 0.08, 0.27). The waypoints must be reached in this order.

phases.name: disturbance_recovery
phases.text: When this phase begins, the environment pushes the ball along world +x for 0.03 s with a fixed impulse (`disturbance_impulse`). The phase completes when all of the following hold for 0.4 s without interruption. Both forks support the tray. The push has been fully applied (at least 95% of `disturbance_impulse`). The ball's centre is within 0.045 m of the tray centre in the tray's x-y plane. The ball moves at less than 0.07 m/s relative to the tray, including the tray's rotation.

phases.name: exit_alignment
phases.text: With both forks supporting the tray, the tray's frame origin is within 0.04 m of (0.12, 0.18), measured horizontally (x and y only).

phases.name: natural_discharge
phases.text: The ball is contained in the basin and does not touch the tray, for 0.7 s without interruption. Contained in the basin means all of the following, in the basin's frame (origin at the centre of its floor's top surface, axes = world axes). |x| and |y| of the ball centre are below 0.0919 m (0.10 - 0.45 x radius; the same bound is used on both axes). Its height above the basin floor is between 0.014 m and 0.0778 m. It has been in contact with the basin within the last 25 ms. Its speed is below 0.09 m/s. Neither fork has to support the tray in this phase, but the tray must still stay above z = 0.17 m. This completes the task.

task_failures: ball_spill: before natural_discharge (in phases shared_support to exit_alignment), the ball leaves the tray region. In the tray's frame that is |x| >= 0.11 m, |y| >= 0.16 m, or a centre at or more than 0.01 m below the tray floor's top surface.
shared_support_drop: at any time, in every phase including the discharge, the tray's frame origin falls below z = 0.17 m.
contact_rules: The forks may touch the tray and the ball, which are free objects, and nothing else: not the basin or its posts, not the table, not the robot pedestals. No other robot part, the fingers included, may touch anything. The two arms and their forks must never touch each other, and a fork must not touch its own arm. The tray and the ball may touch the basin.
world_goals_fixed: Tray waypoints A = (0.12, -0.04, 0.27) and B = (0.02, 0.08, 0.27) apply to the tray's frame origin and are announced at reset as `goal_waypoints`. The exit point (0.12, 0.18) applies in the horizontal plane and is not announced. The tray's frame origin must always stay at or above z = 0.17 m.
difficulty_note: The two arms form a closed chain through a tray that is only loosely cradled, so they must move in lockstep or the tray slips out of a fork. Meanwhile the ball rolls freely in a shallow tray and is pushed once on purpose. The final tilt has to pour the ball into the basin without letting the tray sink below 0.17 m.
standard_notes: Nothing moves at t = 0: the tray rests in both forks and the ball lies still in it. The only scripted motion is the push the ball receives the moment the third phase (disturbance_recovery) starts.
